{"questions": [
{"id": "p1", "topic": "geometry: integer right triangles with a given leg (factor pairs)", "error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the perimeters of the right triangles with integer side lengths that have a leg of length 48.",
"answer": 3576, "target_wrong": 3400,
"error_description": "The factor pair 9·64 of 576 (giving the primitive triangle 48-55-73, perimeter 176) is left out of the list of divisor pairs; every other pair is handled correctly.",
"cases": ["(k,m)=(1,576): 48-575-577, perimeter 1200", "(2,288): 48-286-290, perimeter 624", "(3,192): 48-189-195, perimeter 432", "(4,144): 48-140-148, perimeter 336", "(6,96): 48-90-102, perimeter 240", "(8,72): 48-64-80, perimeter 192", "(9,64): 48-55-73, perimeter 176", "(12,48): 36-48-60, perimeter 144", "(16,36): 20-48-52, perimeter 120", "(18,32): 14-48-50, perimeter 112"],
"solution": "Let the other leg be b and the hypotenuse c. Then c^2 - b^2 = 48^2 = 2304, so (c-b)(c+b) = 2304. The two factors have the same parity and their product is even, so both are even: c-b = 2k, c+b = 2m with km = 576 = 2^6·3^2 and k < m (k = m = 24 would give b = 0). The divisor pairs (k,m) are (1,576), (2,288), (3,192), (4,144), (6,96), (8,72), (9,64), (12,48), (16,36), (18,32), and b = m-k, c = m+k gives the triangles 48-575-577, 48-286-290, 48-189-195, 48-140-148, 48-90-102, 48-64-80, 48-55-73, 36-48-60, 20-48-52, 14-48-50. Each perimeter is 48 + b + c = 48 + 2m, so the total is 10·48 + 2(576+288+192+144+96+72+64+48+36+32) = 480 + 2·1548 = 3576.",
"check_code": "import math\na=48\ntotal=0\nfor b in range(1,a*a):\n    c2=a*a+b*b\n    c=math.isqrt(c2)\n    if c*c==c2:\n        total+=a+b+c\nprint(total)"},

{"id": "p2", "topic": "geometry: integer right triangles with area = 3·perimeter (factor pairs)", "error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the hypotenuse lengths of the right triangles with integer side lengths whose area is numerically equal to three times the perimeter.",
"answer": 267, "target_wrong": 238,
"error_description": "The factor pair 8·9 of 72 is omitted (the list runs 1·72, 2·36, 3·24, 4·18, 6·12 and stops), so the triangle 20-21-29 with hypotenuse 29 is missing.",
"cases": ["(a-12)(b-12)=1·72: 13-84-85", "2·36: 14-48-50", "3·24: 15-36-39", "4·18: 16-30-34", "6·12: 18-24-30", "8·9: 20-21-29"],
"solution": "Let the legs be a ≤ b and the hypotenuse c. For a right triangle the inradius is r = (a+b-c)/2 and the area equals r·s where s is the semiperimeter. The condition area = 3·(perimeter) = 6s forces r = 6, i.e. c = a + b - 12. Substituting into a^2 + b^2 = c^2 gives a^2 + b^2 = a^2 + b^2 + 144 + 2ab - 24a - 24b, so ab - 12a - 12b + 72 = 0, i.e. (a-12)(b-12) = 72. Both factors must be positive (if both were negative, a,b < 12 and c = a+b-12 would be negative or the triangle degenerate). The factor pairs 1·72, 2·36, 3·24, 4·18, 6·12, 8·9 give (a,b,c) = (13,84,85), (14,48,50), (15,36,39), (16,30,34), (18,24,30), (20,21,29); each is a genuine right triangle (e.g. 20^2+21^2 = 841 = 29^2). The sum of hypotenuses is 85+50+39+34+30+29 = 267.",
"check_code": "import math\ntotal=0\nfor a in range(1,1000):\n    for b in range(a,1000):\n        c2=a*a+b*b\n        c=math.isqrt(c2)\n        if c*c==c2 and a*b==6*(a+b+c):\n            total+=c\nprint(total)"},

{"id": "p3", "topic": "geometry: lattice points on a circle (sums of two squares)", "error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many points with integer coordinates lie on the circle of radius 325 centered at the origin?",
"answer": 60, "target_wrong": 56,
"error_description": "The representation 325^2 = 0^2 + 325^2 is dropped: the four axis points (±325,0),(0,±325) are not counted, while the seven representations with two nonzero squares (8 points each) are all listed.",
"cases": ["0^2+325^2 (4 points)", "36^2+323^2 (8 points)", "80^2+315^2 (8)", "91^2+312^2 (8)", "125^2+300^2 (8)", "165^2+280^2 (8)", "195^2+260^2 (8)", "204^2+253^2 (8)"],
"solution": "We need the number of integer solutions of x^2 + y^2 = 325^2 = 105625 = 5^4·13^2. Since every prime factor is ≡ 1 (mod 4), the number of representations r_2(n) = 4·(d_1(n) - d_3(n)) = 4·d(n) = 4·(4+1)(2+1) = 60. Explicitly, 105625 = 0^2+325^2 = 36^2+323^2 = 80^2+315^2 = 91^2+312^2 = 125^2+300^2 = 165^2+280^2 = 195^2+260^2 = 204^2+253^2. The representation with a zero gives the 4 points (±325,0),(0,±325); each of the other 7 gives 8 points (two orders, four sign choices). Total 4 + 7·8 = 60.",
"check_code": "import math\nn=325*325\ncnt=0\nfor x in range(-325,326):\n    y2=n-x*x\n    y=math.isqrt(y2)\n    if y*y==y2:\n        cnt+=1 if y==0 else 2\nprint(cnt)"},

{"id": "p4", "topic": "geometry: lattice points and integer-perimeter right triangles", "error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many ordered pairs of integers (x, y) with 1 ≤ x ≤ 25 and 1 ≤ y ≤ 25 are there such that the triangle with vertices (0,0), (x,0), and (x,y) has an integer perimeter?",
"answer": 22, "target_wrong": 20,
"error_description": "The primitive triple 20-21-29 is missed in the list of Pythagorean leg pairs with both legs ≤ 25, so the two ordered pairs (20,21) and (21,20) are not counted.",
"cases": ["{3,4}", "{6,8}", "{9,12}", "{12,16}", "{15,20}", "{18,24}", "{5,12}", "{10,24}", "{8,15}", "{7,24}", "{20,21}"],
"solution": "The triangle is right-angled at (x,0) with legs x and y, so its perimeter is x + y + sqrt(x^2+y^2), which is an integer exactly when x^2 + y^2 is a perfect square, i.e. (x,y) are the legs of a Pythagorean triple with both legs at most 25. Since the hypotenuse is at most sqrt(2)·25 < 36, we list all Pythagorean triples with hypotenuse ≤ 35 and legs ≤ 25: (3,4,5), (6,8,10), (9,12,15), (12,16,20), (15,20,25), (18,24,30), (5,12,13), (10,24,26), (8,15,17), (7,24,25), (20,21,29). (The triples (16,30,34) and (21,28,35) have a leg exceeding 25.) That is 11 unordered leg pairs, none with equal legs, so there are 2·11 = 22 ordered pairs.",
"check_code": "import math\ncnt=0\nfor x in range(1,26):\n    for y in range(1,26):\n        s=x*x+y*y\n        r=math.isqrt(s)\n        if r*r==s:\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"},

{"id": "p5", "topic": "geometry: squares with lattice-point vertices in a grid", "error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many squares have all four of their vertices among the lattice points (x, y) with 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 and 0 ≤ y ≤ 4?",
"answer": 50, "target_wrong": 47,
"error_description": "The tilted squares inscribed in the full 4×4 bounding box (side vectors (1,3), (2,2), (3,1); 3 squares) are omitted; axis-aligned squares and tilted squares in 2×2 and 3×3 boxes are all counted correctly.",
"cases": ["axis-aligned 1×1: 16", "axis-aligned 2×2: 9", "axis-aligned 3×3: 4", "axis-aligned 4×4: 1", "tilted inscribed in a 2×2 box (vector (1,1)): 9", "tilted inscribed in a 3×3 box (vectors (1,2),(2,1)): 2·4 = 8", "tilted inscribed in a 4×4 box (vectors (1,3),(2,2),(3,1)): 3·1 = 3"],
"solution": "Every lattice square has a square axis-aligned bounding box of side k (1 ≤ k ≤ 4). A k×k box can be placed in (5-k)^2 positions, and it contains exactly k squares: the axis-aligned one and k-1 tilted ones (with one vertex at each of the points dividing a side as j : k-j, j = 1,...,k-1). Hence the count is sum_{k=1}^{4} k(5-k)^2 = 1·16 + 2·9 + 3·4 + 4·1 = 16 + 18 + 12 + 4 = 50. Equivalently: 30 axis-aligned squares (16+9+4+1) and 20 tilted ones (9 with side vector (1,1), 8 with side vectors (1,2)/(2,1), and 3 with side vectors (1,3), (2,2), (3,1)).",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\npts=[(x,y) for x in range(5) for y in range(5)]\ncnt=0\nfor q in combinations(pts,4):\n    d=sorted((p[0]-r[0])**2+(p[1]-r[1])**2 for p,r in combinations(q,2))\n    if d[0]>0 and d[0]==d[1]==d[2]==d[3] and d[4]==d[5]==2*d[0]:\n        cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"},

{"id": "p6", "topic": "geometry: obtuse integer triangles with two fixed sides", "error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the integers c for which there exists an obtuse triangle with side lengths 7, 24, and c.",
"answer": 240, "target_wrong": 218,
"error_description": "The value c = 22 is dropped: for the angle opposite 24 to be obtuse one needs c^2 < 576 - 49 = 527, and 22^2 = 484 qualifies, but the boundary value 22 is left off the list (the range is taken as 18 ≤ c ≤ 21).",
"cases": ["c=18", "c=19", "c=20", "c=21", "c=22", "c=26", "c=27", "c=28", "c=29", "c=30"],
"solution": "By the triangle inequality 24 - 7 < c < 24 + 7, so 18 ≤ c ≤ 30. If c is the longest side, the triangle is obtuse when c^2 > 7^2 + 24^2 = 625, i.e. c ≥ 26, giving c = 26, 27, 28, 29, 30. If 24 is the longest side (c ≤ 24), the triangle is obtuse when 24^2 > 7^2 + c^2, i.e. c^2 < 527, so c ≤ 22 (22^2 = 484 < 527 < 529 = 23^2), giving c = 18, 19, 20, 21, 22. (c = 23, 24 give acute triangles and c = 25 gives a right triangle.) The sum is (18+19+20+21+22) + (26+27+28+29+30) = 100 + 140 = 240.",
"check_code": "total=0\nfor c in range(1,100):\n    s=sorted([7,24,c])\n    if s[0]+s[1]>s[2] and s[0]**2+s[1]**2<s[2]**2:\n        total+=c\nprint(total)"},

{"id": "p7", "topic": "geometry: interior lattice points of a lattice right triangle (Pick's theorem)", "error_type": "misapplied_formula",
"question": "How many lattice points lie strictly inside the triangle with vertices (2,3), (17,3), and (2,13)?",
"answer": 61, "target_wrong": 63,
"error_description": "Uses the shortcut 'a right triangle with legs a and b has (a-1)(b-1)/2 interior lattice points', giving 14·9/2 = 63; that formula requires gcd(a,b) = 1, but here gcd(15,10) = 5, and the hypotenuse carries 4 extra lattice points, so the correct count is ((a-1)(b-1) - (gcd-1))/2 = 61.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "The triangle is right-angled at (2,3) with legs 15 (horizontal) and 10 (vertical), so its area is A = 15·10/2 = 75. The number of lattice points on the boundary is B = 15 + 10 + gcd(15,10) = 15 + 10 + 5 = 30 (each side from one vertex to the next contributes gcd of its coordinate differences). By Pick's theorem A = I + B/2 - 1, so I = 75 - 15 + 1 = 61. (Directly: for x = 3,...,16 the number of interior y is the number of integers y > 3 with 2(x-2) + 3(y-3) < 30, giving 9+8+7+7+6+5+5+4+3+3+2+1+1 = 61.)",
"check_code": "V=[(2,3),(17,3),(2,13)]\ndef strictly_inside(px,py):\n    for i in range(3):\n        x1,y1=V[i]; x2,y2=V[(i+1)%3]\n        if (x2-x1)*(py-y1)-(y2-y1)*(px-x1)<=0:\n            return False\n    return True\ncnt=sum(1 for x in range(0,25) for y in range(0,25) if strictly_inside(x,y))\nprint(cnt)"},

{"id": "p8", "topic": "geometry: lattice points in a disk on one side of a perpendicular bisector", "error_type": "algebra_slip",
"question": "How many lattice points (x, y) satisfy x^2 + y^2 ≤ 100 and are strictly closer to the point (2, 0) than to the origin?",
"answer": 129, "target_wrong": 110,
"error_description": "When expanding (x-2)^2 + y^2 < x^2 + y^2 the cross term is written as -2x instead of -4x, yielding -2x + 4 < 0, i.e. x > 2 (x ≥ 3) instead of x > 1 (x ≥ 2); this drops the 19 lattice points in the column x = 2.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "The point (x,y) is closer to (2,0) than to (0,0) exactly when (x-2)^2 + y^2 < x^2 + y^2, i.e. x^2 - 4x + 4 < x^2, i.e. -4x + 4 < 0, i.e. x > 1. So we count lattice points with x ≥ 2 in the closed disk x^2 + y^2 ≤ 100. For each x the allowed y satisfy y^2 ≤ 100 - x^2: x=2: y^2 ≤ 96, |y| ≤ 9, 19 points; x=3: 91, 19; x=4: 84, 19; x=5: 75, |y| ≤ 8, 17; x=6: 64, 17; x=7: 51, |y| ≤ 7, 15; x=8: 36, 13; x=9: 19, |y| ≤ 4, 9; x=10: 0, 1 point. Total 19+19+19+17+17+15+13+9+1 = 129.",
"check_code": "cnt=0\nfor x in range(-10,11):\n    for y in range(-10,11):\n        if x*x+y*y<=100 and (x-2)**2+y*y<x*x+y*y:\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"},

{"id": "p9", "topic": "geometry: acute integer triangles with a given perimeter", "error_type": "misread_condition",
"question": "How many non-congruent acute triangles have integer side lengths and perimeter 36?",
"answer": 12, "target_wrong": 13,
"error_description": "Counts non-obtuse triangles (a^2 + b^2 ≥ c^2) instead of strictly acute ones, so the right triangle 9-12-15 is included, giving 13 instead of 12.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "Write the sides as a ≤ b ≤ c with a + b + c = 36 and a + b > c, so 12 ≤ c ≤ 17. The triangle is acute iff a^2 + b^2 > c^2. c = 17 (a+b = 19, b ≤ 17): (2,17): 4+289 = 293 > 289 acute; (3,16): 265 < 289 and all smaller b are obtuse. 1 triangle. c = 16 (a+b = 20): (4,16): 272 > 256 acute; (5,15): 250 < 256; the rest obtuse. 1 triangle. c = 15 (a+b = 21): (6,15): 261, (7,14): 245, (8,13): 233 are > 225, acute; (9,12): 225 = 225 right (excluded); (10,11): 221 obtuse. 3 triangles. c = 14 (a+b = 22): (8,14): 260, (9,13): 250, (10,12): 244, (11,11): 242, all > 196. 4 triangles. c = 13 (a+b = 23): (10,13): 269, (11,12): 265, both > 169. 2 triangles. c = 12: (12,12,12). 1 triangle. Total 1+1+3+4+2+1 = 12.",
"check_code": "cnt=0\nP=36\nfor a in range(1,P):\n    for b in range(a,P):\n        c=P-a-b\n        if c<b:\n            continue\n        if a+b>c and a*a+b*b>c*c:\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"},

{"id": "p10", "topic": "geometry: lattice points in a lattice quadrilateral (Pick's theorem)", "error_type": "double_counting",
"question": "How many lattice points lie inside or on the boundary of the quadrilateral with vertices (0,0), (16,4), (12,14), and (2,10)?",
"answer": 140, "target_wrong": 142,
"error_description": "The boundary count is taken as the sum of (gcd + 1) over the four edges, 5 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 14, so each vertex is counted twice (correct B = 10). Pick's theorem then gives I = 134 - 7 + 1 = 128 and a total of 128 + 14 = 142.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "By the shoelace formula with vertices in order (0,0), (16,4), (12,14), (2,10): 2A = |0·4 - 16·0 + 16·14 - 12·4 + 12·10 - 2·14 + 2·0 - 0·10| = |0 + 176 + 92 + 0| = 268, so A = 134. The number of lattice points on an edge from one vertex to the next, counting one endpoint, is gcd of the coordinate differences: gcd(16,4) + gcd(4,10) + gcd(10,4) + gcd(2,10) = 4 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10, so B = 10 (each vertex counted exactly once). By Pick's theorem A = I + B/2 - 1, so I = 134 - 5 + 1 = 130. The total number of lattice points inside or on the boundary is I + B = 130 + 10 = 140.",
"check_code": "V=[(0,0),(16,4),(12,14),(2,10)]\ndef inside_or_on(px,py):\n    for i in range(4):\n        x1,y1=V[i]; x2,y2=V[(i+1)%4]\n        if (x2-x1)*(py-y1)-(y2-y1)*(px-x1)<0:\n            return False\n    return True\ncnt=sum(1 for x in range(-1,20) for y in range(-1,20) if inside_or_on(x,y))\nprint(cnt)"}
]}
